comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme pages establish a coherent 180-EC Biology pathway. Year 1 contains 60 EC of broad compulsory biology, medical-biology, mathematics, statistics and research preparation. Year 2 contains 36 EC of compulsory study and 24 EC of domain-specialisation/elective space. Year 3 contains a 3-EC Biology Essay, 3 EC of Personal and Professional Development, 42 EC of domain-specialisation/elective space and a 12-EC research-department internship. The zero-credit introductory programme and Research Skills requirement remain compulsory but fall outside the 180-EC credit-bearing component list. The generic target offers seven named domain specialisations plus an eighth Free domain for students who do not want to select one domain; that least-specialised official option is selected independently of UCR fit, and its genuine profiling space is preserved rather than filled with invented courses. Review 18 October 2026: the linked Biology course is NWI-FFIL100, not the similarly named FFIL101. Current 2026 catalogue objectives corroborate the ethical part of the prospective overview; a 2027 detailed course specification is not yet available. The displayed external pathway remains explicitly the official provisional 2027–2028 overview, not an adopted cohort regulation. Research Skills and the introductory programme are compulsory non-credit obligations. PPD starts in year 1 and is signed off in year 3. The 66 EC of profiling space remains subject to programme approval and is not wholly unrestricted elective space.

alternatives.label: Biology across organisms, ecosystems & health
alternatives.concept: Study living systems from biodiversity, evolution and ecosystems to cells, biochemistry, human physiology, genetics and disease. Laboratory work, statistics and data analysis support these biological questions; environmental science, sustainability governance and ethics add complementary perspectives.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives substantial weight to organismal and ecological biology and to human health and molecular biology, so the label describes its broad biological span rather than presenting one subfield as dominant.
progression: Life-science, sustainability and biodiversity foundations precede molecular cell biology, laboratory work, ecology, physiology, biochemistry, advanced genetics, disease, pharmacology, environmental science and sustainability governance. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Ecology, climate & environmental biology
alternatives.concept: Study biodiversity, evolution, ecosystems and conservation alongside climate change and environmental systems. Spatial analysis, soils, biogeochemistry and sustainability research connect ecological questions with environmental assessment; governance, justice and resource geoscience provide complementary approaches.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by ecology, biodiversity, environmental science, climate, conservation and sustainability, with methods and governance supporting that biological focus.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in molecular, biomedical, physiological and disease study with climate, conservation, environmental systems, spatial observation, soils, adaptation, sustainable farming and environmental-justice study.
progression: Sustainability, biodiversity, climate and ecosystem foundations precede evolution, conservation, environmental analysis, marine biology, biogeochemistry, spatial methods and advanced sustainability research. Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, Earth Observation, Earth System Science Tools and Earth's Resources. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Human biology, neuroscience & health psychology
alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular biology, human physiology, infection, genetics and disease together with neurobiology and cognition. A substantial psychology strand examines behaviour, mental health, development and assessment. Laboratory work, epidemiology, statistics and research synthesis support this combination; it is not a specialist medical or clinical qualification.
alternatives.labelReason: The molecular/physiological disease core and neuroscience are accompanied by six psychology/methods courses. Naming health psychology makes that substantial strand visible rather than implying a purely medical-biology curriculum.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces ten ecology, evolution, sustainability, conservation and environmental courses with a sequenced brain-and-behaviour, cognition, health psychology, development, diagnosis and research strand; it differs from the environmental route by twenty-two courses.
progression: Life, health, biomedicine, brain and behaviour foundations precede molecular cell biology, laboratory work, physiology, biochemistry, neurobiology, cognition, disease, pharmacology, diagnostics and advanced research. Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior precede every course that formally requires them, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Microbiology, functional genomics and physiological adaptation

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Biology bachelor. The official curriculum offers seven subject-specific domain specialisations and an eighth Free domain explicitly intended for students who cannot or do not want to select one domain. The Free domain is therefore the least specialised official continuation of the broad first-year foundation and is selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest response sustains direct biological inquiry through ecology/evolution and molecular/cellular/human biology, not merely neighbouring science. The second direction changes the focus to ecology, climate and environmental assessment; the third combines human biology and neuroscience with a substantial psychological approach to health and behaviour. Their twelve, ten and twenty-two course differences have substantive purposes. Three alternatives have been implemented. The remaining microbiology/genomics/physiological-adaptation candidate contains valid target interests, but no fourth programme or validated specialist implementation is claimed.

blocks: Both develop evolutionary explanations of adaptation and organismal diversity; UCR covers evolution across taxa rather than concentrating on animal anatomy.
Both introduce biological diversity across organisms and ecological settings.
Both examine ecosystem function and interactions between organisms and their environment.
UCR addresses biodiversity and evolution but has no dedicated plant-evolution and development course in the current catalogue.
UCR offers Human Physiology but no dedicated animal-physiology course.
UCR has no dedicated plant-physiology course in the current catalogue.
Both examine biochemical reactions and molecular mechanisms in living systems.
Both examine molecular and cellular processes, regulation and biological information.
Both examine inheritance and genetic mechanisms; UCR concentrates on molecular pathology and genetics.
Both connect nervous-system biology with behaviour and cognition.

Both directly study human organ systems and physiology. UCR Human Physiology covers homeostasis, organ-system function and integration; its narrower physiological focus does not reproduce all of the external Human Biology component.
UCR studies infection and immunity but does not offer a broad foundational microbiology course.
UCR covers anatomy, physiology and disease but has no dedicated histology course.
UCR has no dedicated microbial-metabolism course in the current catalogue.

Both teach multiple regression and analysis of variance as important statistical methods. Radboud also includes Bayesian testing and diagnostic procedures; UCR additionally covers factor analysis and logistic regression. Partial correspondence, not identical scope or software.

The direct partial overlap is hands-on analysis and visualisation of large datasets, an explicit part of the external programme description. UCR Data Science does not teach genome sequencing, genomic databases or genomic interpretation; the genomic subject remains a substantial difference.

Partial correspondence in normative reasoning: Radboud addresses ethical challenges and responsibility in bioscience; UCR teaches moral theories and practical ethics including animal rights and climate. UCR does not establish the external philosophy-of-science or research-integrity coverage.

Both engage critically with scientific literature and evidence. UCR teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis, including analysis in R; it is not a dedicated biology essay or a primary-data biological research project.
UCR's scheduled programmes use statistics and data-science methods but do not include a dedicated mathematics-for-biologists course.

Radboud requires a separate introductory course in data organisation, experimental design and univariate hypothesis testing. UCR’s single scheduled statistics course is shown against the closer multifactorial Statistics II component.
Radboud explicitly teaches communicating science to non-specialist readers. General academic writing elsewhere in UCR does not establish this dedicated public-science-writing course.
Radboud requires a 12-EC internship in a research department. UCR's standardized optional independent-research element is shown alongside this component.
Both introduce environmental systems and the scientific assessment of environmental problems.
Both develop reflective academic and professional formation across the bachelor programme.

notes.text: The broad UCR option combines ecological and human/molecular biology. The environmental option devotes more study to climate, Earth systems, resources and governance; the human option includes substantial health psychology. None reproduces Radboud’s dedicated plant physiology and development, broad microbiology and microbial metabolism, histology, extensive domain specialisation or required research-department internship. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 EC and is not a guaranteed Biology placement.

audience.programmeDescription: Biology at Radboud University studies living systems from plants, animals and ecosystems to cells, genes, the brain and human health. A broad foundation is followed by domain choices, an essay and a research-department internship. The Free domain allows a broad profile across biology and medical biology.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options pursue biological questions through three different combinations: broad biology, ecology and environmental study, or human biology with neuroscience and health psychology. Shared rows indicate important partial content, not equivalent courses or qualifications. Specialist gaps and the different balance of each option remain important. The Radboud curriculum shown is its provisional prospective overview and may change.

curriculum.limitation: Official prospective overview, subject to change. The 180 EC includes 66 EC of domain and elective choices, subject to programme requirements. The introductory programme and Research Skills are additional compulsory non-credit obligations.
